candidate_a_llm_synthesis.name: LLM Synthesis (OpenRouter Llama 3.3 70B / Mistral Small + Groq)
strengths: Successfully reformulates dense bullet lists into natural sentences
Zero ungrounded hallucinations on approved evidence
weaknesses: Susceptible to provider HTTP 402 billing cutoff and rate limits
Higher latency compared to local deterministic generation
Occasionally drops edge-case exceptions if prompt token budget constrains output

candidate_b_deterministic_task1.name: Deterministic Multi-Chunk Fallback Engine (Task 1 Baseline)
strengths: 100% deterministic and resilient; zero reliance on external APIs
Zero hallucinations; strictly copies approved authoritative policy text
Sub-500ms execution latency with zero operational cost
weaknesses: Cannot perform calendar math (e.g., date arithmetic for warranty windows)
Outputs verbatim markdown sections rather than tailored customer replies
Subject to intent routing misclassification in older router versions

candidate_c_improved_full_agent.name: Aster & Row Full Agent (Top-8 Hybrid Retrieval + Fixed Routing + LLM Fallback Cascade)
strengths: Highest overall claim recall (77.94%) across all 50 difficult scenarios
Fixed intent hijacking: policy inquiries route cleanly to KNOWLEDGE rather than false CLARIFY/HANDOFF
Zero hallucinations, 100% structural citation validity, graceful failover under quota exhaustion
weaknesses: 25 cases remain incomplete due to strict multi-criteria conditions and calendar arithmetic limits

selection_verdict.selected_architecture: Aster & Row Full Agent with Resilient Fallback Cascade
selection_verdict.justification: The multi-tier fallback architecture combines the semantic synthesis quality of Llama 3.3 70B with an unbreakable local deterministic safety net. When provider quota was exhausted (HTTP 402), the agent experienced zero downtime, 100% valid citations, zero hallucinations, and achieved 77.94% claim recall with 50.0% fully complete answers on 50 curated difficult customer scenarios.
